newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen mixed to firm at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen mixed to firm at open.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to open mixed to firmer on Tuesday, helped by strength in European markets and the belief that Federal Reserve policy makers would leave U.S. interest rates unchanged at a meeting which starts today.

But stocks and bonds would keep a wary eye on the National Association of Purchasing Managers report for June, due at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, for signs of strength in the manufacturing sector, which might fuel inflation, analysts said.

"I think we're in for a firm open," Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities said. "The European markets are very strong. Plus, we had a lot of confusion at the close yesterday, when end of quarter programs hit...we should see some retrieval out of that."
In early trade, the Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was up 2.45 points at 892.80, while the long bond was down 2/32 at a 6.79 percent yield.
European stock exchanges were higher, partly helped by a stronger dollar which raised prospects for cheaper exports.
On Monday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average finished down around 15 points at 7672.79. The trading session was extremely choppy as the second quarter drew to a close.

But while signs pointed to a higher stock market open, a stronger-than-expected National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) report could revive inflation fears ahead of the Fed meeting, sending markets lower, analysts said.
It was forecast to show a reading of 56.4 in June compared with a reading of 57.1 in May.
"The number to watch today is the NAPM," Wachtel said.

"While Wall Street is looking for a slight decline, given what happened yesterday with the Chicago Purchasing Managers Index -- which showed a surprising uptick -- this is an area of big uncertainty," he said.
A steep rise in the Chicago manufacturing data sent stocks and bonds reeling on Monday.

But even if the NAPM data were strong, the Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee, which starts its two-day meeting today, was still likely to leave rates alone, said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Borwn and Catherwood.
"People are starting to look towards the next Fed meeting," he said.
Analysts said technology stocks could come under some pressure on Tuesday, after an earnings warning from computer chip maker Cyrix Corp.
Auto stocks might also sag over concerns about rebates and the possibility of weaker sales, Wachtel said.
Japan's Nikkei average closed off 429.44 points at 20,175.52, ahead of the FOMC meeting in the United States.
In London, the FTSE 100 was up 64.3 points at 4668.9. U.S. auto and technology stocks were quoted lower in London.
The dollar was up against the yen in Tokyo, trading at 115.08/18 yen. In Europe, the dollar was steady against the mark, trading at 1.7457/62 marks.

The Wall Street Journal said in its Heard on the Street column that Polo Ralph Lauren Corp's stock made a strong start when it debuted with its initial public offering, but it has been mostly downhill for the stock since then.

The New York Times said in its Market Place column that many stocks made big moves just as the closing bell rang on Monday. It said some traders thought some of the action may have involved a bit of end-of-quarter performance enhancement.
((Wall Street desk 212-859-1730))
